data.narrative:
Vertical Semiconductor is a Seed-stage semiconductor design company founded by Joshua Perozek, Cynthia Liao, and Tomas Palacios. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of eight private peers in Chips & Semiconductors at Seed/Series A stages, plus three public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD), including recent private valuations of SambaNova Systems ($11.0B Series A), Rebellions ($2.3B Series A), and d-Matrix ($2.0B Series A).

Two methods proved applicable. Stage-Progression anchors to the company's $11M total raised and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, implying $28M. Peer-Median triangulates across the three same-sector comparables, yielding a median valuation of $2.3B (range: $2.0B–$11.0B). Public-Comp Anchoring was not applied; the sector P/S median for public semiconductors is 20.5x, but the target's revenue is undisclosed, precluding reliable application of this method.

The triangulated analysis across two methods supports a range of $23M (low) to $2.7B (high), with a median of $1.2B. The wide spread reflects stage mismatch: Stage-Progression assumes a near-term funding event, while Peer-Median captures Series A valuations. Key uncertainties include whether Vertical's technology roadmap justifies Series A peer multiples at Seed stage, and actual revenue trajectory remains unobserved.
